subject: divide(a, b) utility function in example.js (4 lines)

findings.description: No type checking on a or b. Non-number arguments get coerced silently: divide('6', '3') returns 2, divide('a', 1) returns NaN, and divide(1, '0') skips the zero guard because '0' !== 0 and returns Infinity.
findings.fix: Validate inputs up front, e.g. if (typeof a !== 'number' || typeof b !== 'number') throw new TypeError('divide expects numbers'); or add TypeScript/JSDoc types.

findings.description: NaN inputs go straight through and return NaN without an error. The b === 0 check does already catch -0, because -0 === 0 is true.
findings.fix: If NaN results should be rejected, add Number.isNaN checks (or Number.isFinite for both operands) and document the behavior.

findings.description: A generic Error is thrown for division by zero, so callers can only tell it apart from other errors by matching the message string.
findings.fix: Throw a RangeError, or a custom DivisionByZeroError, so callers can check it with instanceof.

summary: Clean, correct division helper with an explicit zero guard; the only gaps are minor input-type validation and edge-case handling.
